sort imports like proHello fellow developers,
Do you ever browse through a GitHub repository only to find a messy, unorganized block of imports? It can be incredibly frustrating to decipher which modules are being used when the code looks disorganized.
While working on a recent personal project, I found an effective solution to this problem: automating import sorting using the `eslint-plugin-import` extension. This tool helps keep your imports tidy, consistent, and easy to read.
Here is how you can implement it:
Step 1: Install the plugin
Run the following command in your terminal:
npm i eslint-plugin-import
Step 2: Configure ESLint
If you already have ESLint set up, add the following configuration to your eslint.config.js file:
// Import plugin recommended rules
…importPlugin.flatConfigs.recommended.rules,
…importPlugin.flatConfigs.typescript.rules,
// Resolver-dependent rules are disabled due to TS resolver incompatibility
'import/namespace': 'off',
'import/default': 'off',
'import/named': 'off',
'import/no-unresolved': 'off',
// Custom rules
'import/order': [
'warn',
{
groups: [
'builtin',
'external',
'internal',
'parent',
'sibling',
'index',
'object',
'type',
],
'newlines-between': 'always',
alphabetize: {
order: 'asc',
caseInsensitive: true,
},
},
],
'import/no-duplicates': 'error',
'import/first': 'error',
'import/newline-after-import': 'error',
'import/no-cycle': 'warn',Step 3: Integrate with lint-staged
Add the linting process to your lint-staged configuration to ensure imports are automatically sorted before every commit.
Step 4: Verify
Add a new commit to your repository to test that the imports are now automatically formatted according to your new rules.
Happy coding!
